original_question: Is the global Seshadri constant epsilon(X) = inf{epsilon(L) : L in Pic(X) is ample} positive for every smooth projective surface X?
target_in_paper: Section 3.6, the unnumbered question quoted from Demailly [10, Question 6.9]: whether the global Seshadri constant epsilon(X) is positive for every smooth projective surface X.
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper's actual target. It matches the unnumbered question in Section 3.6 almost verbatim: it uses the same invariant epsilon(X) = inf{epsilon(L) : L in Pic(X) ample} and asks the same positivity question for every smooth projective surface X.
missing_details: The draft does not define epsilon(L). To make the question stand-alone, one should say that epsilon(L) is the least Seshadri constant of L, i.e. epsilon(L) = inf{epsilon(L,x) : x in X}.
The draft does not define epsilon(L,x). For a self-contained formulation, one should specify epsilon(L,x) = inf{(L.C)/mult_x(C) : C subset X an irreducible curve through x}.
The phrase 'L in Pic(X) is ample' should be stated explicitly as 'L is an ample line bundle on X'.

The ambient field/characteristic is left implicit in the draft; Section 3.6 states the question without a characteristic restriction, while the nearby implication from bounded negativity is only formulated in characteristic zero.

The nearby context in Section 3.6 also introduces the stronger pointwise quantity epsilon(X,x) = inf{epsilon(L,x) : L in Pic(X) ample}; this is not the target question itself, but it is part of the paper's immediate motivation and should be mentioned in justification.
refined_question: Let X be a smooth projective surface. For an ample line bundle L on X and a point x in X, define epsilon(L,x) := inf{(L.C)/mult_x(C) : C subset X is an irreducible curve passing through x}, and define epsilon(L) := inf{epsilon(L,x) : x in X}. Is the global Seshadri constant epsilon(X) := inf{epsilon(L) : L in Pic(X) is ample} always strictly positive?
justification: The draft is already aimed at the correct place in the paper: the unnumbered question in Section 3.6 quoting Demailly's Question 6.9. It should not be replaced by the stronger neighboring problem about epsilon(X,x), because the paper explicitly presents that only as additional nearby context. The main refinement needed is to make the notation epsilon(L) and epsilon(L,x) explicit so the question is mathematically stand-alone. The immediate paper context is that Section 3.6 introduces the pointwise invariant epsilon(X,x) and Proposition 3.6.1 shows that Conjecture 3.3.1 (Bounded Negativity) would imply epsilon(X,x) > 0 in characteristic zero, even giving an effective lower bound via the blow-up Y = Bl_x(X).
